I really want to like this game, but I just can't really recommend it at this time. It feels like it's an early access title, without having the early access treatment. Most common bug I ran into repeatedly was enemy pawns could capture units that were in the space right next to them, while moving forward diagonally (IE they have pawn in B4, you move a pawn to A4, they move their pawn to A3 and take your pawn that's in A4) without any modifiers listed that do this. I've seen the game do a few other illegal moves as well, but if I try to do it it won't let me. The shop feels overly bloated with things you can get, which then makes getting anything assembled feel insanely difficult. I do like that you can freeze things in the shop for later purchase, but even after just a few rounds on the easiest difficulty, the AI will have advantage in pieces unless you get really lucky in what the shop gives you, and that you have the money to buy anything useful.

imagine chess but with a really annoying ai that drags on every match and plays defensively 24/7. also this is a roguelike and there's a million matches edit: i feel like i need to add more feedback here because after thinking on it for a bit there's a few decisions that confuse me By far the most important thing in this game is your board setup and the moment you choose a match to play you can no longer move your board around. I don't really understand why there's no "planning" phase when you start a match. If you're not squinting your eyes at your screen at the tiny UI showing the enemy's setup then you are effectively just throwing. Please. Just let me move my board around when I go into a match. I don't really understand the three choices given for matches. Why is there an "easier" board and a "harder" board? I guess for risk/reward but it just feels frustrating when you first get into the game. Did I lose the boss because I didn't choose the challenging boards, and thus ruin my eco? Should I be choosing the challenging boards for more money? Why would I not choose the challenging boards if it gives me 50% more money? I am throwing if I don't choose the more rewarding board. etc etc. I don't know I just don't get why the choice exists. It would feel infinitely more purposeful if the two choices had similar difficulties but you chose them based off of which board feels more suited to your setup. I mean, like, it's not like you're given the choice of an easier boss or a harder boss. So why does this choice exist? The archer sucks. Why does upgrading my rook give me the archer? There's a lot of tactile feel from upgrading your pieces but I felt so unbelievably trolled when upgrading my rook turned it into the archer! Balatro (on steam, at least) shows a 11.7% achievement rate for Gold Stake, the highest difficulty. This game has a 12.7% achievement rate for the very first setup (which by the way, why the hell is the courtesan the default setup and not just... an easy to understand setup that gives you an immediate boost? The duck setup is easily the best setup for beginners. It's simple and gives you immediately strong pieces. I really cannot overstate how difficult this game is for very meager rewards. I imagine the response will just be "get good" but even if I got good the game feels like it has very little to actually sink my teeth into. The upgrades/badges are kind of nards. Every coin causes your turn to pass for whatever reason. The game feels like it's balanced around PvP... even though I'm fighting a damn AI the entire time. The game quickly fatigues you and falling asleep for a mere moment can instantly spiral the game out of your control. There's too much going on and I just can't keep track of it all. The AI never fatigues. I feel just frustration playing this game.

自从《小丑牌》横空出世以来，一种新的游戏种类出现了，一般称之为“小丑牌like”，典型作品就是《青天井》和《我地麻》，而随着《passant》的出现，我更愿意将这类游戏称之为“棋牌rogue like”，他为我们拓宽了思路，除了德州、麻将外，我们还能把哪些经典棋牌类游戏和rogue like缝在一起呢？我希望我能在一年后玩到rogue中国象棋，rogue五子棋，rogue军旗，rogue飞行棋，rogue跳棋，rogue uno，rogue 斗地主。再拓宽一点，rogue斯诺克能不能搞？计算机的出现带来了便利的伪随机，古代智者发明围棋享受“公平”的互相博弈，而我们又何尝不能改变古人的这些“公平”的发明，改成“不公平”的充满随机性的人机对弈呢？在如今这个时代，传统的棋牌游戏对于游戏经历丰富的一部分玩家已经不能够满足他们的娱乐需求，但当我们将rogue加入其中，会不会唤醒我们童年时，和家人一起坐在桌子前，轮流出牌下棋的回忆呢？ —————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————— 说回这款游戏，国际象棋rogue，我是一名除了知道国际象棋规则以外，完全不会各种技巧、各种牌谱的玩家。我从出生至今下过的国际象棋可能不超过10局。 这款游戏对我来说有一定的挑战，不像小丑牌和青天井、我地麻一样秒上手。因为我对各种棋子的特性、弱点完全不知道。但游戏的难度确实给了我快速适应的空间。我面对的对手是由单一种类开始的。我一开始要思考如何对付对方的双象，后来我发现可以想办法兑掉黑色格子上的象，另一个象就无法影响到白色格子上的棋子，我就利用白格子推进、升变。然后在逐步面对马、车。 也有十分有新鲜感的东西，例如马和象的缝合怪——公主，马和王的缝合怪——龙骑士，卒和王的缝合怪——兵。 如果你喜欢《小丑牌》、《我地麻》，略懂一些国际象棋，我会推荐你试一试，实在不行两小时退款嘛。 现在我已经慢慢入手了这款国际象棋rogue，也许再体验一段时间后我还会再次来评价。

Enjoy chess? Enjoy roguelike games? Ever wanted to feel like MacReady from John Carpenter's The Thing when he pours his whiskey into the chess computer because playing against an AI designed specifically to beat you can more often than not be infuriating? Play Passant! A wonderful combination of your run-of-the-mill chess, combined with what I can only describe as pure flavour. Want Archduke Ferdinand in chess? He's there. How about a duck? Passant has it. But what about... a cannon? Oh yes, there's a cannon. There are so many pieces and methods to discover, that you wouldn't have been able to think of them in your wildest dreams. What I appreciate most about it, is that after playing it for so long and using certain pieces, you start to learn new ways of playing, you start to instinctively recognise what moves you can make. You can design your board in a way that you believe will ensure victory, only to have made an error and get checkmate'd in one fell swoop. But better yet, you start to actually predict what moves the AI is going to make after so many repeated rounds of doing it. This game is fantastic, but not for the impatient. I know, because I've gotten every achievement, and it took a LOT of patience, but the payoff is phenomenal. Also if you really wanted to, and you just want a standard chess simulator to play against a grandmaster level chess AI? You can do that too. The game is a labour of love for chess and roguelike games, give it a go!

The AI is very much just a basic chess engine designed to protect itself from the players attacks, and not lose material value in trades. It plays defensively and tactically for normal chess. The problem with that is that when the player wins after forcing drawing tactics, and a good chess player notices this, its highly exploitable and no longer fun. Finding ways to force trade downs to instantly win when neither player has material, or finding annoying repetitive checking tactics that the AI does nothing to avoid (and would rather walk into than lose material) shouldn't be a win condition for the player. I won a majority of my games by checking the king back and forth for six moves because the AI refused to play a sub-optimal engine move and would rather lose to the repetition win con....that's pretty sad.

先说下背景吧，我下国际象棋已经有三年了，这么多年来steam 上的chess游戏我多多少少都看过，没有让我特别喜欢的，要不就是换个皮，本质还是那一套，或者就是靠情色吸引人的，但是这个游戏真的让我眼前一亮，我是前阵子在油管上看到有人玩的时候才入坑的，当时看的时候觉得挺简单的，只要会下应该都没问题，但是我实际上完了才发现，这个游戏难度真不低，我是1500分的选手，所以我选了提高难度，也就是第二难的那个难度，AI的水平真的不低，虽然不会弃子或者很强的战略，但是用我不熟悉的棋子能和我杀个难解难分，好多次我都需要悔棋才能通过，（尤其是那个像王一样走的兵，真的像变态一样），基本上的逻辑还是想同的需要杀王，但是它多了一个可以连续多次将军来获胜的方式，这个真的对残局下的不好的玩家很友好，由于每次开局的棋子都不同，所以他这主要考验的是中盘的能力，对于我这种局面性的棋手，真的有种说不出的压力，最后通关的时候真的好险23333，总而言之，如果你喜欢象棋的话，这游戏你一定要试一下，不会吃亏的。

Of the many roguelikes I've played, this one is by far the simplest and easiest. If you have a foundational understanding of chess, regardless of AI intelligence, it is free to win game. Once you realize how to set up your board pre-blind, it becomes questionably simple. You end up taking multiple free pieces at the start, sometimes checkmating midgame boards with two rooks on hand. Some items are boring and so niche there's no point, while others are unquestionably the most broken thing you've ever used. My third game was literally copy making queens, to the point that I had fifteen queens and one king. The game currently needs desperate balance to feel like an enjoyable roguelike, instead of "look for the same three items after you econ early".

I liked some things about this game, but ultimately I can't bear how hard it is to see what's going on. It should have a 2D board option, but it doesn't. On the 3D one it's hard to tell pieces from other modified ones that are similar. It needs a 2D board with clean icons, and like 180% the size of the current 3D board. I played for like 90 minutes and my eyes feel tired. Difficulty in this game just means throwing more stuff at you, for example, the level I lost in had like nine rooks and six knights, and I had like three rooks, four knights and eight bishops. It's cool for a few games, but then it gets old fast, because it gets more crowded but that doesn't necessarily mean that you can do new cool things; you just have to do the same thing as in the previous level but for longer. I spent a while thinking about how to fix this, but I couldn't come up with anything; it's clear that something is missing, but it's hard to say what exactly. Some parts of the UI are sort of a Balatro clone, but they look cheap, like drawn on Paint or something. The effects of the pieces and badges are not super interesting, and they don't interact with each other to make cool stuff happen; it's mostly pretty bland. I've had this on my wishlist for months and was sure I'd like it, but it's like the game is incomplete. Bosses don't feel like bosses. 'Floors' don't feel different to the previous one. Your options to buy and play stuff don't increase a lot as you climb levels... It feels like 75% of a game, but the other 25% is the one that was gonna make it fun.

It is chess Balatro, but with actual chess. Unlike Balatro which tosses out most of the game it is based on, in Passant you still play chess. It borrows mostly the random Roguelite upgrades and stage system from Balatro. There are more win conditions than normal, such as winning by consecutive checks or taking all non king pieces, etc., and of course fairy pieces/mechanics. You also have the ability to set up your starting positions, so you can live your fantasy of having queens/rooks on the second row. It can be fun to set up a one/two move checkmate, though these only happen in the early stages usually.

Turning chess into a roguelite is a tough premise, because the skill difference in chess players is huge. If your game is 95% chess then grandmaster level players will breeze through your game without having to interact with your roguelike mechanics at all, and at that point they might aswell play chess. If the roguelike mechanics are so powerful that chess noobs can rely on them for support, and playing correct moves is no longer important, then your game becomes just about the metagame and the chess is trivialized. At the end of the day Passant suffers from the same issue, but until you've figured out all the mechanics it's actually a great game. You have to play decent chess in the early game, where material is equal, and you have to interact with roguelike mechanics because your opponents will have 70 points of material in the later game. Once you've figured out which items are good then it's just chess again though, so for me it's back to chess.com. All in all 7€ well spent though -- Passant is probably my favourite chess roguelite, on par with Usurper.
